name: Tax Refund Notice
summary: Confirms that the Tax Authority owes you money for a tax year and shows how and when the refund will be paid.

guidance.primaryNextStep: Check that the refund amount and bank details are correct, then monitor the payment window before following up.
guidance.deadlineSummary: The transfer is usually made by the date or processing window shown
guidance.appliesWhen: the Tax Authority says you overpaid and plans to send money back
guidance.recommendedChannel: Use the refund inquiry channel printed on the notice if the transfer is delayed or the bank details changed.
guidance.whenToContactAuthority: the bank account is outdated, the amount seems wrong, or the refund does not arrive in the stated window
guidance.whatToVerify: Verify the tax year, refund amount, receiving bank account, and expected transfer timing.

sections.explainer: Tax year — tells you which year the refund calculation applies to. Make sure it matches the period you expected to review.
Refund amount — the sum the Tax Authority believes should be returned to you after offsets, credits, and prior payments are taken into account.
Bank account details — shows where the refund will be sent. If the account is closed or belongs to the wrong person, the transfer can bounce or be held.
sections.actionRequired: Check the account number carefully and update it immediately if it is outdated.

sections.explainer: Transfer timing — gives the expected payment window or the next processing date. Refunds can take longer if identity or banking details still need validation.
sections.deadline: The transfer is usually made by the date or processing window shown

sections.explainer: Inquiry or correction — explains how to contact the office if the amount looks wrong, the bank details have changed, or the refund has not arrived.
sections.actionRequired: Contact the office if the refund is missing after the stated window and keep the letter number ready.
